transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-07 | 09:00 PDT / 16:00 UTC | Duration ~48m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Rivera (Redwood SE), Dr. Aisha Rahman (Cobalt - Head Infra), Tom Bowers (Cobalt - Security), Liam Chen (Cobalt - AI Ops), Nadia Ortiz (Cobalt - Regulatory)

Summary: High-level discovery for running Redwood Private in a fully sequestered cluster. Key concerns: offline update process, approved media, hardware parity vs hosted models, signed images, patch windows, compliance artifacts (SOC2/ISO/21 CFR), and network egress controls.
Topics: offline update workflow, HSM/KMS for key management, hardware constraints (NVLink/PCIe), maintenance windows, canary/fallback in air-gapped environments, acceptance testing for model quality, rollback strategy, shipment of physical media.
Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.app/secure/airgap-playbook (shared: airgap-playbook.pdf), internal perf spreadsheet (link shared in chat)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round of intros then we'll jump in. i'm maya, redwood, AE. devon is our systems engineer.
[00:12] Dr. Aisha Rahman: hi, i'm aisha, head of infra at cobalt. good to meet you.
[00:16] Tom Bowers: tom, security lead. we run in a sealed cluster, no egress to internet.
[00:20] Devon Rivera: hey, good to be here. i'll mostly talk hardware and the update flows.
[00:25] Liam Chen: liam, ai ops — i manage our inference workloads and monitoring.
[00:28] Nadia Ortiz: nadia, regulatory — i have a few questions around auditability and data residency.
[00:32] Maya Chen: awesome. main goal for today is to understand constraints so we can map hosted/dedicated/private options to what you can actually do on-prem. aisha, can you walk us through the sequestered cluster layout?
[00:45] Dr. Aisha Rahman: sure. two racks, isolated VLANs, no outbound routing. management plane is on a physically separate network. we have a locked lab where images are staged. GPU-wise we're testing a single RTX 6000-x and have access to a 4xA100 test node at our colo. storage is on NFS behind a firewall, and we do hardware change control with a paper trail.
[01:10] Devon Rivera: ok, so that's helpful. the two big things for us are: first, how you want to handle updates to runtime and models when there's no internet; second, perf delta between your local GPUs and what our cloud profiles assume.
[01:25] Tom Bowers: for updates we require signed images, signatures verified with our H S M. we do not accept USBs unless they've been forensically sealed and logged. sometimes we ship via locked courier with checksum manifest.
[01:38] Maya Chen: got it. redwood supports signed images and we can integrate with customer K M S / H S M for key verification. our private deployment packaging can be exported as an OCI image and signed; we can also produce an offline bundle with checksums and PGP if you prefer.
[01:55] Dr. Aisha Rahman: yeah the signing is non-negotiable. also we need to know the patch window — we can't have long downtime. what's your suggested strategy for rolling patches in a sealed environment?
[02:10] Devon Rivera: in air-gapped we do a staged rollout: image distribution to an import node, smoke-tests in a staging ring (non-prod), then production nodes one rack at a time. because KV cache warm-up is significant, we recommend canary traffic routed to local test harness to warm caches. note: warming caches without production data can skew perf numbers.
[02:35] Liam Chen: warming cache is a huge ask. our token costs spike if we do synthetic warmups. can you do pre-warmed checkpoint bundles?
[02:43] Devon Rivera: yes, we can produce a pre-generated KV checkpoint for a given prompt set; however it's sensitive since it's derived from model state. the safer option is to warm with a representative prompt corpus that you provide, run locally.
[02:57] Tom Bowers: about telemetry: we cannot allow outbound logs. we expect an audit log that we host locally and periodic exports via physical media. is redwood able to disable any phone-home?
[03:10] Maya Chen: absolutely. in private deployments we can disable outbound telemetry and provide on-demand diagnostic bundles that you pull and ship. we also offer an optional data-diode style forwarder if you ever want one-way telemetry out under strict control.
[03:26] Nadia Ortiz: from a regulatory standpoint we need evidence of chain-of-custody for updates, and a trace of who approved a rollout. can you integrate with our S S O and ticketing for approvals?
[03:38] Devon Rivera: we support SAML for SSO and can tie rollout approvals to an external ticketing webhook or a signed approval artifact. we can also emit RBAC events into your SIEM.
[03:49] Dr. Aisha Rahman: let's talk hardware compatibility — we have an RTX 6000-x in prod. any expectations around performance delta vs a100?
[03:58] Devon Rivera: RTX6000-x will be somewhat slower for large context lengths; a100s with NVLINK and larger HBM will do better at sustained throughput. we can run a compatibility probe and give token/sec and p50/p95 latency estimates. realistically you should expect 20-40% lower throughput on the 6000-x for dense 8k contexts, but single-request latency for small prompts should be comparable.
[04:20] Liam Chen: what about quantization and mixed-precision — do you support int8 runs that could help us on 6000-x?
[04:27] Devon Rivera: yes, we support quantized execution paths and optimized kernels that help on consumer/prosumer cards. tuning the batch size and kv memory settings is essential; we'll provide recommended config files.
[04:38] Tom Bowers: storage wise, do you require local SSD for model mmap? our infra policy prohibits NVMe on some nodes.
[04:45] Devon Rivera: model mmap performance benefits from local fast storage; if NVMe is not an option we can run from network storage but will see latency variance. we can also provide a compact model variant with smaller working set.
[04:58] Maya Chen: quick Q — do you have compliance constraints beyond SOC2? e.g., 21 CFR part 11 or ISO 27001?
[05:06] Nadia Ortiz: yes, we need 21 CFR evidence for audit trails and paper logs for updates, and we're pursuing ISO 27001 next quarter.
[05:15] Maya Chen: ok we'll surface our 21CFR artifacts and change-control process. we'll add the audit trail export details to the shared pack.
[05:22] Dr. Aisha Rahman: how do you handle fallback if a new model or runtime causes regressions? we can't call home to access older variants.
[05:31] Devon Rivera: good question. for private/offline we recommend: 1) immutable image tags for runtime and model, 2) keep a rollback image in your import node, 3) staged canaries, and 4) we can ship a minimal fallback image you import and can switch to manually. we can also provide a conservative model family specifically for sequestered nodes.
[05:53] Liam Chen: what about canary traffic routing? we do not have a complex service mesh.
[05:58] Devon Rivera: we can include a small sidecar router that runs locally and routes a percentage of traffic to canaries; it does not require external control plane. the routing rules are static files you can update via your internal CI.
[06:10] Tom Bowers: patch cadence — we usually have quarterly maintenance windows. can redwood bundle cumulative patches vs frequent micro patches?
[06:18] Maya Chen: yes, we can produce cumulative images you only import on your quarterly cadence. security patches are flagged and we can provide CVE mapping and severity so you can triage.
[06:27] Dr. Aisha Rahman: about model quality — we run regulated inference and need deterministic outputs in some flows. how do you handle repeatability and seed control?
[06:36] Devon Rivera: we have deterministic runtime options and can pin RNG seeds per request. however for large models sampling and temperature affect outputs; we can provide locked deterministic configs for regulatory use cases.
[06:47] Nadia Ortiz: audit-wise we need transcripted request/response hashes, not raw payloads. can that be done?
[06:54] Devon Rivera: yes, we can emit salted hashes of inputs and outputs into your local audit logs so you can prove behavior without storing PHI.
[07:03] Maya Chen: quick note — we will not move you to hosted; this is purely for private sequestered deployment. we'll map features accordingly.
[07:10] Dr. Aisha Rahman: fine. what about licensing model for private — flat fee plus support or usage-based?
[07:16] Maya Chen: for sequestered private we typically do a platform license + support and an optional reserved capacity fee if we manage dedicated pools. for your case, since it's fully managed on-prem by you, it'll be license + optional premium support. i'll send pricing options.
[07:29] Tom Bowers: legal will want indemnity language around model outputs — we will need to review those clauses.
[07:34] Maya Chen: understood, include legal in next steps.
[07:37] Liam Chen: can we run a short perf probe with our internal prompts? i can drop a node in our lab and you'd run the profiler?
[07:45] Devon Rivera: yep — we'll produce a small probe tool you run as a container that uploads only metrics to the local bundle. no egress needed; metrics can be pulled and we can read them on-site or you can share the tarball.
[07:58] Dr. Aisha Rahman: curious about backup/restore for models — how big are bundles and what's recommended?
[08:05] Devon Rivera: depends on model. a 7B quantized model might be tens of GB, a 70B full model hundreds. we can provide delta patches so you don't reship entire image for minor updates.
[08:18] Maya Chen: quick clarification on keys — do you want Redwood to sign artifacts or do you want to manage signing end-to-end?
[08:25] Tom Bowers: we want to manage signing. redwood should support verifying our signatures during import.
[08:30] Devon Rivera: that's supported — we document the signature format and integrate verification into the import tool.
[08:36] Dr. Aisha Rahman: anything about monitoring? we need SLO alerts locally.
[08:41] Maya Chen: the private console can run entirely on-prem and generate local alerts; we can map alert hooks to your pager/ops.
[08:47] Liam Chen: do you have any reference customers in regulated pharma who've done end-to-end?
[08:52] Maya Chen: we can share redacted case studies — we've done sealed clusters for a couple of med-device customers, i'll get permissioned references.
[09:00] Nadia Ortiz: for acceptance we'll need a runbook and an acceptance test set; can redwood provide a template?
[09:07] Devon Rivera: yes, we'll supply an acceptance test harness and a sample prompt set; you can sign off on pass/fail metrics.
[09:13] Tom Bowers: one more on supply chain: do you provide SBOMs for runtime components?
[09:18] Maya Chen: yes, we provide SBOMs and CVE reports for components in the image.
[09:22] Dr. Aisha Rahman: ok good. sounds like next steps are pretty clear.
[09:25] Maya Chen: recap: we'll share the airgap playbook, SBOMs, 21CFR artifacts, and a draft commercial term. devon will run the hw compatibility probe and produce perf numbers. tom will share your patch window doc and nadia will list regulatory acceptance criteria. we'll target the guided run the week of May 18.
[09:43] Tom Bowers: yes i'll email the patch window and the sealed chain-of-custody template.
[09:46] Liam Chen: i'll prepare a small prompt corpus for warming.
[09:49] Dr. Aisha Rahman: thanks. one last tiny thing — do you have a recommended hardware baseline for production?
[09:55] Devon Rivera: for production at scale we'd recommend at least 4xA100 per inference pool for high throughput; for smaller regulated workloads a pair of RTX6000-x with quantized models can be acceptable. we'll include a sizing calculator in the probe results.
[10:08] Maya Chen: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts and the commercial draft.
[10:13] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: a few proper nouns may be misrecognized (H S M, NVLink sometimes as 'N V link'), timestamps approximate.
